source-integrity.name: provenance and freshness
source-integrity.basis: Primary operating evidence is current through 2026-09-10 and independent market evidence through 2026-09-26; issuer backlog/growth claims are not counted as independent corroboration.

structural-causal.name: crossDivisionLeverage
structural-causal.basis: Oracle can combine cloud infrastructure with database/application relationships to capture workloads across its stack.

structural-causal.name: bottleneckControl
structural-causal.basis: OCI capacity is scaling rapidly but remains dependent on upstream power, chips, networking and datacenter delivery.

structural-causal.name: scenarioRobustness
structural-causal.basis: Large contracted demand improves visibility while capital intensity and long-duration conversion create downside sensitivity.

discovery-weak-signals.name: AI/cloud infrastructure exposure
discovery-weak-signals.basis: triple-digit IaaS growth and very large RPO indicate accelerating infrastructure demand

adversarial-red-team.name: capitalIntensity
adversarial-red-team.basis: Rapid datacenter expansion can depress returns if capacity is delivered ahead of economic demand conversion.

adversarial-red-team.name: concentrationRisk
adversarial-red-team.basis: The source establishes large RPO but does not disclose concentration within new AI commitments.

adversarial-red-team.name: competitiveResponse
adversarial-red-team.basis: OCI competes against larger hyperscale ecosystems and customer self-build options.

adversarial-red-team.name: confidenceInflation
adversarial-red-team.basis: Backlog/RPO should not be treated as cash realization without conversion evidence.

expectations-execution.name: capacity execution
expectations-execution.basis: physical capacity delivery accompanied strong revenue and earnings growth

thesisQuality.basis: Triple-digit IaaS growth, $664b RPO and an entrenched database/application estate support exceptional demand durability, tempered by capital-conversion risk.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Q1 revenue grew 30%, cloud 62%, IaaS 121% and GAAP EPS 55%, representing broad operating acceleration.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: Current growth-adjusted valuation offers strong headroom if execution persists, but remains exposed to mega-cap capacity and financing risk.

catalystScore.basis: RPO conversion, continued capacity delivery and rapid OCI growth are multiple material source-supported catalysts with visible operating linkage.

governancePower.basis: Strong strategic execution and long-duration leadership are constructive, while aggressive capital deployment and concentrated insider influence temper governance confidence.

alignment2036.basis: Cloud compute, databases and AI infrastructure are foundational capabilities across multiple plausible 2036 enterprise and technology futures.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: OCI, database, ERP, HCM, health and other applications reuse enterprise relationships and data infrastructure across multiple independent demand engines.

bottleneckControl.basis: Oracle controls meaningful database/workload placement and fast-growing OCI capacity, but upstream power/chip/network constraints and competing hyperscalers prevent unique bottleneck status.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Enterprise software plus infrastructure diversify demand, while AI-capacity concentration, financing and large-contract conversion create scenario sensitivity.

substitutionResilience.basis: Deep database/application integration creates switching friction, though competing hyperscalers and customer self-build remain credible alternatives.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Oracle demonstrated 850MW capacity delivery, but rapid OCI expansion remains materially dependent on power, accelerators, networking and datacenter construction capacity.

pricingPower.basis: Entrenched enterprise software plus accelerating cloud economics support strong value capture, while hyperscaler competition and large contracts constrain exceptional pricing claims.

riskEvidence.basis: Material risks are capital intensity, opaque concentration within very large RPO, upstream infrastructure constraints, hyperscaler competition and long-duration contract conversion.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Current operating and backlog facts come from fresh primary results and valuation is independently current; confidence is reduced by undisclosed RPO concentration and incremental-capital returns.

scoreRecord.thesis: Oracle is converting entrenched enterprise software relationships into rapidly scaling AI/cloud infrastructure demand with extraordinary contracted visibility, while capacity intensity and RPO concentration remain the main underwriting constraints.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: Massive capacity investment and long-duration RPO fail to convert into attractive cash returns because power/chip constraints, concentration or hyperscaler competition weaken economics.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Further OCI capacity deployment and evidence that the $664b RPO converts into sustained cloud revenue and cash returns.
